recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. If future context corrections are needed, make them in the FHIR Extension Pack and evaluate them against FHIR-43033 and its follow-up history rather than reintroducing removed core extension-definition files.
issue_request: FHIR-34304 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core request, raised against R4 and applied for R5, to allow most Questionnaire appearance/behavior extensions to be declared on ElementDefinition so reusable question-library elements can carry those properties into generated Questionnaires.
initial_application: The Jira comment points to commit 00afa6314b4db439e283b1a6400ce44eb42198a8, which added ElementDefinition context declarations to 20 source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-extension-questionnaire-*.xml files in the R5 core source.
additional_context: The current FHIR core checkout no longer contains those extension-definition files; commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 removed extension definitions from R5 source. The current definitions live in the FHIR Extension Pack. Later Published issue FHIR-43033 reviewed the same Questionnaire extension context problem, restored ElementDefinition context where valid after contextInvariant validation problems, and intentionally dropped ElementDefinition context for questionnaire-fhirType, questionnaire-maxOccurs, and questionnaire-minOccurs because ElementDefinition already has corresponding elements.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current core Questionnaire source remains active and accurately describes propagation for extensions that have both ElementDefinition and Questionnaire.item contexts, while the actionable extension context declarations are outside the core checkout and already reflect the later FHIR-43033 decision.
